# Italian School of San Diego

A small education business has many connected workflows: students, families, teachers, schedules, payments, documents, and regulatory records. Andrea uses that direct operating experience to design practical automation.

::: {.ai-section}
## One business, connected systems

::: {.ai-checks}
- Enrollment records connected to the correct class and communication workflow
- Calendars aligned with schedules, locations, teachers, and students
- Payment status connected to receipts and follow-up tasks
- Employee hours prepared from approved calendar and operational records
- Customer inquiries researched before a response is drafted
- Transactions matched with receipts and supporting documents
:::

The useful lesson is not a particular software product. It is the operating model: define an authoritative source, automate repeatable preparation, keep a visible record, and require human approval before consequential actions.

::: {.ai-policy}
The same controls apply across the system. Calculations and drafts can run automatically. Sending, submitting, scheduling, changing records, and initiating payments wait for approval from a responsible person.
:::
